# Panasonic Microwave Not Heating (H98)

One note first: "H98" is a well-known Panasonic inverter microwave error code, not just a model name. If your display shows H98 (or H97) when it stops heating, that points to a specific fault.

## What H97/H98 Usually Means
• H98: The inverter board isn't detecting proper current to the magnetron. Usually a failed inverter board or magnetron.
• H97: Similar, often pointing more toward the magnetron.

## Things You Can Safely Try First
1. Power reset: Unplug it for 5–10 minutes, then plug back in. Sometimes clears a one-off glitch.
2. Use a dedicated outlet: No extension cords or power strips. Low or unstable voltage can trigger H98, especially on circuits shared with a kettle, toaster, etc.
3. Water test: Heat 1 cup of water for 1 minute on high. If it barely warms, the heating system has truly failed.
4. Check the door: Make sure it closes firmly and latches properly. Faulty door switches can cause heating issues.

## If That Doesn't Work: The Likely Culprits
| Part | Approx. cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Inverter board | $50–150 | Most common cause of H98 |
| Magnetron | $40–100 | Second most common |
| Door switches / thermal fuse | $5–20 | Less common for this code |

Many people replace the inverter board first since it's the most frequent failure, but if the magnetron is the real problem, the new board can fail again. A technician can test both.

## ⚠️ Safety Warning
Microwave internals can hold lethal voltage even when unplugged. The inverter board has capacitors that store charge. Don't open the case unless you have experience with high-voltage electronics and know how to discharge it safely.

## Repair or Replace?
If the microwave is older or was inexpensive, a professional repair (parts + labor, often $100–200+) may approach the cost of a new one. If it's a higher-end or built-in model, repair is usually worth it.

Is the microwave actually displaying H98, or is that the model number? And does it still run (light, turntable, fan) just without heating? That'll help narrow it down further.
h98 is what the screen says when it stops; the model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ. fan and turntable start then it beeps and stops

Thanks, that confirms it. Your NN-CD87KSBPQ is a UK-market inverter combination microwave (microwave + grill + convection), and the behaviour you describe is the classic H98 pattern.

## What's Happening
When you start a microwave cycle, the fan and turntable come on, then the control board tries to power the magnetron through the inverter. It doesn't detect the expected current, so it shuts down for safety and shows H98. This means the problem is almost certainly in the microwave heating circuit: the inverter board, the magnetron, or (less often) the wiring or connector between them.

## Quick Checks Before Paying for Repairs
1. Unplug for 10+ minutes, then try again. This occasionally clears it if the fault was triggered by a power blip.
2. Plug directly into a wall socket on a circuit not shared with a kettle or toaster. No extension leads.
3. Test the grill and convection modes on their own (no microwave power). This is the most useful diagnostic:
• Grill/oven heats normally → the problem is isolated to the microwave circuit (inverter or magnetron).
• Grill/oven also fails → more likely a control board or power supply issue.
4. Never run it empty while testing. That can damage the magnetron further.

If H98 still appears after a reset on a dedicated socket, it's a hardware fault and won't fix itself.

## Likely Parts (UK Prices, Approx.)
| Part | Cost | Likelihood |
|---|---|---|
| Inverter board | £50–120 | Most common cause |
| Magnetron | £30–70 | Second most common |
| Connector/wiring fault | Minimal | Occasionally a loose or burnt connector on the inverter |

A technician should test the magnetron (a simple resistance check) before replacing the inverter. A faulty magnetron can cause a new inverter to fail.

## Repair or Replace?
• Professional repair: typically £100–180 including parts and labour.
• New equivalent combi microwave: roughly £200–350.

Since the CD87 is a fairly well-built 34L combi, repair is often worth it if the quote is under about £150, especially if the grill and convection still work fine.

## Worth Checking
• Warranty: If it's relatively new or you bought an extended warranty, contact Panasonic UK or the retailer first.
• Consumer Rights Act: If it's only a few years old and failed early, you may have a claim against the retailer even outside the manufacturer's warranty.

## ⚠️ Safety Reminder
The inverter board and magnetron circuit carry lethal voltages and can stay charged after unplugging. Unless you're experienced with high-voltage electronics, leave the inside to a qualified repairer.

Does the grill or convection mode still heat? That will narrow it down a lot.
yes grill heats fine. so is it worth fixing? it was about £300

Good news: since the grill works, the control board and power supply are fine. The fault is isolated to the microwave circuit (inverter board or magnetron), which keeps the repair contained.

## Short Answer
Usually yes, if the repair quote is £150 or less and the microwave is under about 7–8 years old. A comparable new combi costs £200–350, and the rest of yours is working.

## Before Paying Anything, Check These
1. Warranty: Panasonic UK, the retailer, or an extended warranty (e.g., Currys Care, John Lewis) may still cover it.
2. Consumer Rights Act 2015: If it's only a few years old, you may have a claim against the retailer. A £300 appliance should reasonably last more than 2–3 years. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland you can claim up to 6 years after purchase (5 in Scotland), though after the first 6 months you may need to show it's an inherent fault.
3. Home insurance: Some policies cover appliance breakdown.

## Decision Guide
| Situation | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Under warranty / recent purchase | Claim, don't pay |
| Quote £100–150, under ~7 years old | Repair, good value |
| Quote £150–200 | Borderline, depends on age and condition |
| Quote over £200, or 8+ years old | Replace |

## Tips for Getting It Repaired
• Ask for a fixed quote that includes diagnosis, and ask whether the call-out fee is deducted if you go ahead.
• Make sure they test the magnetron before replacing the inverter. Fixing only the inverter when the magnetron is faulty is the most common reason this repair fails twice.
• Ask whether parts are genuine Panasonic and whether the repair has a warranty (3–12 months is typical).

## DIY Option
If you're experienced with electronics, the inverter board is a fairly simple swap (about £50–120 for the part). But the high-voltage capacitors can hold a dangerous charge after unplugging, so only do this if you know how to discharge them safely. Otherwise, the labour cost is worth paying.

How old is it roughly? That's the main factor in whether a warranty claim or repair makes the most sense.

## Verdict: Worth Repairing, If the Price Is Right

At 6 years old, a well-built combi like the CD87 typically has several more years in it. The grill, convection, controls and power supply all work, so you'd only be fixing one isolated fault.

Rough rule for your situation:
| Repair quote | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Under £120 | Repair, clear win |
| £120–150 | Repair, still reasonable |
| Over £150 | Lean towards replacing |

A new equivalent will cost around £200–350, so paying much over £150 for a 6-year-old unit stops making sense.

## Check This First: Your Purchase Date
You're right at the edge of the Consumer Rights Act limit (6 years in England, Wales and NI; 5 in Scotland).

• If it's just under 6 years, you may still have a claim against the retailer. At this age you'd need to show the fault is inherent rather than wear and tear, which can be hard. But a retailer may offer a goodwill repair or partial refund, especially for a £300 appliance. Find your receipt or order confirmation and act quickly.
• If it's just over, that route is likely closed. Also check any extended warranty or home insurance appliance cover.

## If You Repair It
• Get a fixed quote including diagnosis.
• Insist they test the magnetron before fitting a new inverter board.
• Ask for a warranty on the repair (ideally 6–12 months).
• Panasonic's own repair service, or an independent repairer using genuine parts, are both fine. Independents are often cheaper.

## If You Replace It
Since the grill and oven still work, you could keep using it as a small oven/grill in the meantime, so there's no rush to buy.
